<feature feature-id="CC-0068">
  <title>Fix updateStatus to preserve original reconcile error</title>
  <description># GitHub Issue #186: Fix updateStatus to preserve the original reconcile error

**Category**: refactoring | **Scope**: Small

**Description**: In keystone_controller.go:139-145, when r.Status().Update() fails, the original reconcileErr is discarded and only the status update error is returned. Refactor updateStatus to use errors.Join or a multi-error pattern that preserves both the original reconcile error and the status update error, ensuring the root cause is always visible in controller logs.

**Motivation**: When a reconcile fails AND the subsequent status update also fails, the root cause of the original failure is silently lost. This makes debugging production issues significantly harder because the logs only show 'failed to update status' without any indication of what actually went wrong.

**Affected Areas**:
- `operators/keystone/internal/controller/keystone_controller.go`

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- [ ] Both the original reconcile error and the status update error are returned when both fail
- [ ] Controller logs contain the root cause error, not just the status update failure
- [ ] Unit test verifies error preservation in the dual-failure case
- [ ] Single-failure cases (reconcile fails, status succeeds and vice versa) still work correctly

**Labels:** enhancement

---
Source: https://github.com/C5C3/forge/issues/186</description>
  <tasks>
    <task status="pending">1.1 Refactor updateStatus to use errors.Join and add unit tests for all error combinations (REQ-001, REQ-002, REQ-003, REQ-004)</task>
    <task status="pending">2.1 Update keystone-reconciler reference doc to describe error joining behavior (REQ-005)</task>

  </tasks>
  <implementation-notes>The fix is a 2-line change in updateStatus: (1) add 'errors' to imports, (2) replace `return ctrl.Result{}, fmt.Errorf("updating status: %w", err)` with `return ctrl.Result{}, errors.Join(reconcileErr, fmt.Errorf("updating status: %w", err))`. When reconcileErr is nil, errors.Join(nil, statusErr) returns statusErr (Go spec: nil arguments are discarded). When both are non-nil, the joined error's Error() returns both messages separated by newline. Controller-runtime logs the returned error, so both errors will appear in controller logs automatically. For tests, use interceptor.Funcs{SubResourceUpdate: func(ctx context.Context, c client.Client, subResourceName string, obj client.Object, opts ...client.SubResourceUpdateOption) error { return fmt.Errorf("simulated status update error") }} to inject status update failures. Call updateStatus directly (not via Reconcile) for focused unit tests.</implementation-notes>
</feature>
